paraphrase: Victory to the congregational chanting of Kṛṣṇa's names, which cleanses the mirror of the mind, extinguishes the forest fire of worldly existence, spreads the moonlight of welfare, is the life of the bride of knowledge, increases the ocean of bliss, gives a taste of full nectar at every step and bathes the whole self.

original.text: ceto-darpaṇa-mārjanaṃ bhava-mahā-dāvāgni-nirvāpaṇaṃ śreyaḥ-kairava-candrikā-vitaraṇaṃ vidyā-vadhū-jīvanam | ānandāmbudhi-vardhanaṃ prati-padaṃ pūrṇāmṛtāsvādanaṃ sarvātma-snapanaṃ paraṃ vijayate śrī-kṛṣṇa-saṅkīrtanam ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: You have made many names and placed all your powers in them, with no fixed rule of time for remembering them; such is your mercy, O Lord, yet such is my misfortune that I have no attraction for them.

original.text: nāmnām akāri bahudhā nija-sarva-śaktis tatrārpitā niyamitaḥ smaraṇe na kālaḥ | etādṛśī tava kṛpā bhagavan mamāpi durdaivam īdṛśam ihājani nānurāgaḥ ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: Humbler than a blade of grass, more tolerant than a tree, giving respect to others and not expecting it for oneself — so should one always sing (the names of) Hari.

original.text: tṛṇād api sunīcena taror api sahiṣṇunā | amāninā mānadena kīrtanīyaḥ sadā hariḥ ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: I desire neither wealth, nor followers, nor beautiful women, nor poetry, O Lord of the world; may there be causeless devotion to you, my Lord, birth after birth.

original.text: na dhanaṃ na janaṃ na sundarīṃ kavitāṃ vā jagad-īśa kāmaye | mama janmani janmanīśvare bhavatād bhaktir ahaitukī tvayi ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: O son of Nanda, consider me, your servant fallen into the terrible ocean of existence, by your mercy as a particle of dust at your lotus feet.
speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: When will my eyes stream with tears, my voice falter and choke, and my body bristle with horripilation as I take your name?
speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: In separation from Govinda a moment seems an age, my eyes pour like the rains, and the whole world seems empty.

original.text: yugāyitaṃ nimeṣeṇa cakṣuṣā prāvṛṣāyitam | śūnyāyitaṃ jagat sarvaṃ govinda-viraheṇa me ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D

speaker: Caitanya

paraphrase: Let him embrace me, devoted to his feet, or trample me, or break my heart by not appearing; let that libertine do as he likes — he alone, and no other, is the lord of my life.

original.text: āśliṣya vā pāda-ratāṃ pinaṣṭu mām adarśanān marma-hatāṃ karotu vā | yathā tathā vā vidadhātu lampaṭo mat-prāṇa-nāthas tu sa eva nāparaḥ ||
original.edition: recalled from the standard text (skeleton); verify in Phase D
